whyUs.title: SEO-informed from the start
whyUs.description: Every piece is written with keyword intent in mind. We don't retrofit SEO. It's built into the brief, the structure, and the copy.

whyUs.title: Voice matching that holds up
whyUs.description: We don't write generic content. We write in your client's voice. A discovery brief, a tone audit, and we match it close enough that your client reads it back to you.

whyUs.title: Fast turnaround, consistent quality
whyUs.description: Most deliverables turn around in 3 to 5 business days. Retainer partners get predictable delivery dates, every month, on time.

faq.question: How do you match the client's voice?
faq.answer: We start with a voice and tone brief: existing content samples, audience descriptions, and a short Q&A. The first deliverable includes a voice reference doc you can reuse across all future content.

faq.question: Do you include revisions?
faq.answer: Yes, two rounds of revisions are included on every piece. Additional rounds are available if needed. In practice, most clients pass on round two.

faq.question: Can this be combined with SEO?
faq.answer: It's the strongest combination. Content without SEO strategy targets the wrong terms. SEO without content can't rank. Order both from the catalog, or your account manager will flag the bundle when it fits.

faq.question: What industries do you write for?
faq.answer: We work across the industries your clients serve: local services, e-commerce, SaaS, professional services, and more. The voice-matching process handles the niche specifics.

faqExtra.question: Is the content AI-generated?
faqExtra.answer: No. Every piece is written by a human writer and passes an editor review plus originality checks before delivery. We may use AI for research assistance, but the writing your client receives is human — that's the whole point of the voice guarantee.

faqExtra.question: What counts as one piece?
faqExtra.answer: One blog post or article up to ~1,500 words, one landing page, or one email sequence of up to five emails. Bigger scopes (pillar pages, long-form guides) are quoted as multiples — your quote lists every piece before you commit.

faqExtra.question: Can you hold a monthly publishing schedule?
faqExtra.answer: Yes — that's what the retainer is for. Each client gets a monthly content calendar, briefs are approved up front, and delivery dates are commitments you can pass on to your client.

faqExtra.question: Who owns the content?
faqExtra.answer: Your client, fully. All drafts, final files, and publishing rights transfer with delivery — no license-back, no reuse by us, ever.
